clue.text: They operate on the head, though they're not brain-surgeons

definitions.text: They operate on the head, though they're not brain-surgeons

parts.words: They operate on the head, though they're not brain-surgeons
parts.note: operating on the head sounds surgical, but here it means working on what grows on top of it: cutting and styling

explanation.surface: A joke about people who work on heads without being neurosurgeons.
explanation.definitionFit: Salon stylists cut and style the hair on clients' heads, a joking sort of operation.

clue.text: Debates about price-fixing

parts.note: read not as policy arguments over cartels but as a buyer and seller arguing to settle a price

explanation.surface: Arguments over illegal price-fixing by companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargaining over cost at a market stall is a small debate that fixes the price.

clue.text: Some quite miserable people set out

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some rather unhappy people depart.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'people set out' does not mean the answer; only 'set out' (list item by item) does, and 'people' is surface padding. 'Some' signals the letters hidden across quITE MISErable.
explanation.definitionFit: To list something point by point is to set it out item by item.

clue.text: Bring accusations after the underworld boss is let off

indicators.note: after says the accusations piece is placed following the underworld piece

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
to charge someone is to bring accusations against them

explanation.surface: Charges are laid once a gangland boss walks free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster; here it is Dis, Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun that is fired, or a prisoner released, is let off: both senses fit.

clue.text: The painter may well need to take such a stand

definitions.text: The painter may well need to take such a stand

parts.words: The painter may well need to take such a stand
parts.note: taking a stand sounds like adopting a firm position, but it is the literal frame an artist rests a canvas on

explanation.surface: An artist may have to adopt a firm position on something.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist props the canvas on a wooden stand in the studio.

clue.text: Clean up for example as punish ment

parts.note: to scour is to clean by hard scrubbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the example abbreviation is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Being made to scrub up is offered as a form of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints the definition split as 'punish ment'. In this down entry 'up' means read upwards; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip, or anything that causes great suffering, serves as an instrument of punishment.

clue.text: A particular honour

definitions.meaning: a particular point or detail, as in 'in every particular'
to honour someone is to hold them in high esteem

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a detail ('in that regard') and esteem or deference shown to someone.

clue.text: The return journey

parts.note: not the trip home, but a trip whose route returns to its own starting point

explanation.surface: Just the trip back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip that ends where it began loops back on itself.

clue.text: Singers making an entrance

indicators.note: making says the letters of the word before are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Performers walking onto the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in, an entry or way in.

clue.text: A personal voucher

parts.note: a voucher sounds like a coupon, but here it is a person who vouches for another

explanation.surface: A coupon for one person's use.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer guarantees or answers for someone, vouching for them personally.

clue.text: Revival as a result of one trio's grim resolution

indicators.note: resolution is read as breaking down into parts and rearranging, so the letters before it are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, its S included

explanation.surface: A comeback brought about by three people's stern determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 letters of ONE TRIOS GRIM are rearranged; 'as a result of' is a link. The name is the 19th-century movement for Italian unification.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for resurgence names the nineteenth-century movement that unified Italy.

clue.text: Neck with an attractive girl when it's not too warm

parts.note: a col is a neck or pass between mountain peaks
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: Kissing a pretty girl on a chilly day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' looks like a verb for kissing; it is a col, a narrow mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat chilly weather is a little cool rather than warm.

clue.text: The distribution of gifts needs great craft

parts.note: large means great in size
SS (steamship) is a vessel, a craft

explanation.surface: Handing out presents requires a lot of skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill; it is a ship, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving of money or presents is a bounty handed out freely.

clue.text: The trainee is left a direction? That's a yarn!

parts.note: L is the learner plate, a trainee driver
taken as written
E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A fanciful story about a novice being given directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a yarn' sounds like disbelief at a tall story; it is a literal thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, hard-twisted cotton thread used for stockings.

clue.text: Judge a reader should be at the back of the car

definitions.text: at the back of the car

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game
a lector is one who reads aloud, as in church

explanation.surface: A referee who reads aloud belongs in the back seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear safety reflector bounces headlight beams back so following drivers see the vehicle.

clue.text: Alfresco meal for a flier?

parts.note: alfresco means in the open air, out in the field
fare is food, the stuff of a meal

explanation.surface: Picnic food offered to a bird or a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: An alfresco meal is 'field fare'; the definition 'a flier' is a bird, a thrush of the winter countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: This large thrush visits Britain in winter, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Draw back, or deer etc will get agitated

indicators.note: agitated says the letters of the words before are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Retreat, or the deer and other animals will become nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare verb means to move backwards or return to an earlier place.

clue.text: Big fellow backing superior — the queen

parts.note: a titan is a giant, a big fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue backing says the superior abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, superior, written AI

explanation.surface: A giant supporting someone of higher rank, namely the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support; it reverses AI to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: She is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: He spends his days dealing with the complaints of viewers

definitions.text: He spends his days dealing with the complaints of viewers

parts.words: He spends his days dealing with the complaints of viewers
parts.note: complaints of viewers sounds like a TV broadcaster's inbox, but means eye ailments of those who see

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's staffer who fields grumbles from the audience all day.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor treats disorders of sight, the ailments of those who look.

clue.text: An island in mid-Atlantic — a primates paradise

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A mid-ocean isle that is heaven for apes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are concealed across atlantiC A PRImates; 'paradise' is surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian isle lies in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Once-fashionable city

parts.note: chic means stylish, fashionable
ago means in the past, once

explanation.surface: A town that used to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once-fashionable' reads as one adjective meaning dated; split it into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Illinois metropolis sits on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Hawkers may invest five hundred pounds in fruit

indicators.note: invest means to wrap or surround, so the fruit encloses the money letters

parts.note: pears are fruit
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Street sellers might put five hundred pounds into fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' looks financial; here it means to clothe or surround, putting DL inside PEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling sellers who peddle goods door to door are street traders.

clue.text: Beats striking cricket scores

parts.note: workers on strike are out
runs are the points scored in cricket

explanation.surface: Industrial action beats cricket scores.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone in a race is to be faster than them.

clue.text: Droop by an authoress from France

parts.note: to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: Wilting next to a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Françoise Sagan was a French novelist, author of Bonjour Tristesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Françoise Sagan was the French novelist of Bonjour Tristesse.

clue.text: Get dunderhead to twist before the French weaken

indicators.note: before says the twist piece comes ahead of the French article

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter
to wind is to twist
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Make a fool turn round before the French grow weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like an insult but is read as 'dunder-head', its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to shrink or diminish gradually.

clue.text: Telephone about an object splitting

indicators.note: about says the telephone word goes round the object word

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A phone call concerning a thing that is breaking apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' means a goal, END, not a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rending means tearing apart, ripping in two.

clue.text: A mother, a six-footer and very hard

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
an ant is an insect, with six feet

explanation.surface: A mother, plus one tall person, and very tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; an insect has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding in resolve, like the legendary hardest stone.

clue.text: Having to undo a knot sure can make one bad-tempered

indicators.note: undoing the words before unravels their letters into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Struggling to unpick a knot can make anyone irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and quarrelsome, always ready to argue.
